entries.name: BDNF Val66Met
entries.summary: T (Met66) allele lowers activity-dependent release of BDNF, a growth factor for neurons. Linked to slightly weaker episodic memory and a smaller hippocampus in some studies; links to depression and anxiety are inconsistent. Exercise raises BDNF whatever the genotype.

CT.label: Val/Met, possibly slightly weaker episodic memory

entries.name: KIBRA rs17070145
entries.summary: T allele carriers performed better on episodic memory tests in the original and several replication studies; the effect is small and not found in every cohort.

entries.name: FKBP5 rs1360780
entries.summary: T allele slows the shut-off of the cortisol stress response. In people with childhood adversity it is linked to higher PTSD and depression risk (a gene-environment interaction); alone it predicts little.

CT.label: slower cortisol recovery; matters mainly after trauma

TT.label: slower cortisol recovery; matters mainly after trauma

entries.name: CACNA1C rs1006737
entries.summary: Genome-wide significant risk allele for bipolar disorder and schizophrenia, each A copy raising odds only ~1.1–1.2x. Lifetime risk stays low for almost every carrier; useful for research, not prediction.

entries.name: ACTN3 R577X
entries.summary: T (577X) is a stop codon: XX people make no alpha-actinin-3 in fast-twitch muscle fibres. RR is over-represented among sprint and power athletes, XX slightly among endurance athletes. Training matters far more.

entries.name: COL1A1 Sp1 (rs1800012)
entries.summary: A allele (the 's' allele, T on the gene's strand) alters type I collagen production; meta-analyses link it to lower bone density and more osteoporotic fractures, and to some ligament injuries. Weight-bearing exercise, calcium and vitamin D matter more.

AA.label: ss, lower bone density, ~1.8x vertebral fracture odds
